s1.syndrome_frame: Acute hypoxemic respiratory failure following a high-altitude snow burial with airway obstruction
salient_findings: Bilateral rales and crackles on pulmonary auscultation
Low oxygen saturation despite supplemental oxygen
key_facts: Patient was buried under snow at 2500 m above sea level
Hand remained exposed, leading to quick discovery and excavation
Patient never lost consciousness
Patient recalled being unable to breathe due to compacted snow blocking airways
Patient was cyanotic but conscious upon excavation
Patient denied hitting any rocks or objects during burial
Oxygen saturation was 93% on 100% oxygen via mask
Initial hemoglobin was 168 g/L, decreasing to 135 g/L on day 1
CT scan showed extensive macular alveolar infiltrations throughout both lungs
Pulmonary function tests were normal 4 weeks post-incident
Echocardiography was normal 4 weeks post-incident

shortlist.label: High-altitude pulmonary edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was buried under snow at high altitude and showed signs of respiratory distress

shortlist.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had frank haemoptysis, bilateral rales and crackles on pulmonary auscultation, and low oxygen saturation

shortlist.label: Reperfusion injury
shortlist.why_kept: Patient experienced a period of hypoxia followed by reperfusion, which can cause lung injury

shortlist.label: Aspiration pneumonia
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had compacted snow blocking his airways, which may have led to aspiration

shortlist.label: Hypothermia-induced pulmonary edema
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was buried under snow and may have experienced hypothermia, which can cause pulmonary edema

raw.rationale: The patient was buried under snow at 2500 m above sea level, which is a high-altitude environment, and presented with symptoms such as cyanosis, tachypnoea, and frank haemoptysis, which are consistent with high-altitude pulmonary edema. The CT scan findings of extensive macular alveolar infiltrations throughout both lungs also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Acute respiratory distress syndrome
rejected.why: While the patient presented with similar symptoms, the specific context of high-altitude exposure and the lack of any other clear precipitating factor make high-altitude pulmonary edema a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Reperfusion injury
rejected.why: There is no clear evidence of ischemia or reperfusion in this case, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Aspiration pneumonia
rejected.why: The patient did not have any oral bleeding wounds or other signs of aspiration, making this diagnosis unlikely.

rejected.label: Hypothermia-induced pulmonary edema
rejected.why: While hypothermia could be a contributing factor, the patient's primary issue appears to be related to the high-altitude environment rather than hypothermia alone.
